Senses.Explanation: To turn or return (回) in reciprocal relation (互): mutual interchange. The corpus provides a compact self-gloss in the lines 'the objects at every gate interchange and do not interchange; turning, they further enter into one another; otherwise each remains in its position' (門門一切境，回互不回互，回而更相涉，不爾依位住). This wording permits both relation and distinct position rather than reducing the term to simple fusion. Caoshan says ordinary feelings and holy views must interchange (直須回互). In Caodong usage upright and crooked (正偏), light and dark (明暗), or guest and host (賓主) can mutually interchange; one later address expands the guest-host deployment as each containing the other and the two exchanging positions without a fixed rank.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 1,249 occurrences in 253 texts. The exact contrast 'interchange and do not interchange' (回互不回互) occurs 91 times in 54 texts; its gloss 'turning, they further enter into one another' (回而更相涉) occurs 40 times in 33 texts. The old gloss 'guests and hosts changing places freely' described only one deployment and was too narrow for the headword.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), Yongjue Yuanxian's commentary on the Agreement of Difference and Unity (參同契註). Yongjue Yuanxian quotes and begins to explain the defining contrast: things interchange and do not interchange; turning, they further enter one another, or else remain in position.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: 二隱謐禪師語錄, hall address raising Linji's guest-and-host exchange. Eryin Mi is the exact speaker of the stored comment: he says that even clearly distinguished guest and host still await and reciprocally interact with one another, then demands their interpenetration and interchange.
